findings.claim: With a named test still red alone plus an unnamed section failure, a like-for-like named base replay that is green yields own of the subject for the section too, though the section never ran on that tree.
findings.evidence: Probe through ClassifyRed (go test -overlay): Failed [internal/foo TestX, section/audits], Alone red with same selectors, Replays [{main, Named green}] -> Cause{own, subject, Tests [internal/foo TestX, section/audits (package)]}. red.go:64 like-for-like suppresses the Whole fallback; red.go:140 a named run never reproduces an unnamed unit.
findings.change: Non-gating now (no production caller until U1a2a; whole base run through U1a2b). For U1b: the caller declares the whole/section run as Named while an unnamed unit remains, or the like-for-like exception applies only when no unnamed unit remains.
findings.relation: new; rule: design D1 row 4, an unnamed failure replays its failed package or section

findings.claim: A rerun red only for a test it did not select, with a like-for-like green base, yields own of the subject with an empty Cause.Tests and the named test listed as flaked.
findings.evidence: Probe: Alone red naming internal/foo TestOther, base Named green -> Cause{own, subject, Tests []}, Flaked [internal/foo TestX].
findings.change: Non-gating; U1b's words name the rerun's failures when Cause.Tests is empty.
findings.relation: new; rule: design D5, the stop names its tests

findings.claim: RedEvidence has no field for the check's own report completeness (as part A1 specifies), and an empty Failed with a green replay yields own with no tests.
findings.evidence: Probe: RedEvidence{Goal subject, Replays [{base, wrapper green}]} -> Cause{own, subject, Tests []}. A1's types omit the check report's completeness; U1a2a maps unreadable evidence to CannotRun.
findings.change: Non-gating; U1a2a's caller never classifies a red with no failed unit.
findings.relation: new; rule: design D1, the evidence holds whether the check's report is complete

findings.claim: T1's own invariant requires Whole.Complete, stricter than production, so a future row with a green wrapper whole fallback for a named test would fail spuriously.
findings.evidence: red_test.go:120 checks replay.Whole.Exited && replay.Whole.Complete && replay.Whole.Passed; red.go:45 complete() accepts Wrapper. Probe: named fallback to wrapper whole green -> own (correct). No current row is affected.
findings.change: Non-gating; if U1b adds such a row, the invariant uses complete().
findings.relation: new; rule: T1's invariant mirrors production's completeness rule (a Wrapper run is complete by its exit)
